So happy to see Docusaurus hit the big 2.0! I use it to power my blog and it's a tremendous tool. The DX is fantastic and it's open source! I've been able to contribute to it myself.
I've been using Docusaurus for a few years now and it's my top choice for making small-mid sized websites. Dark mode out of the box is a killer feature!
Think I'll leave it for a while, Meta is so poisonous.
Scroll up and down that page and you see about 30 MB of resources downloaded. Yikes.

I was hoping for something I could use to generate my docs, but this is so incredibly over-engineered... React components, MDX, TypeScript config files, CSS-in-JS? Do you really need all that to write docs?
I searched the documentation for "pdf" and did not find anything relevant - is it really true that this is not able to generate a PDF from the written text?
Been using Docusaurus for quite a while... I would say though that part of what appealed to me does seem to be getting lost - the simplicity... it is becoming a bit of a buzzword beast.
I introduced Docusaurus as the way to finally unite all documentation for our project and it has been a huge success... migrating from that to a Docusaurus site was really easy.
has been a very very long journey, but Docusaurus has rightfully earned its place as the default docs engine for most dev focused companies and startups and OSS libraries.

I haven't used Starlight, but Docusaurus is very slow. The last time I used it, its performance on a large documentation site was terrible, even causing the GitHub Actions Runner to time out. In other words, a single build took over 30 minutes.

To be completely honest: The reason I looked for another documentation framework was that I was fed up with Docusaurus taking forever to start the initial development server... I remember waiting over 20 seconds for the development server to start, which really frustrated me.
For writing technical styled documentation, I've found fumadocs to be amazing... We just moved to it from Docusaurus and couldn't be happier.

Long time user of (and contributor to) Docusaurus. I use it to build my markdown powered tech blog. It is very much a Goldilocks product for me ("just right") in that it has React support, Markdown support, TypeScript support.

Overall, I think Docusaurus is great. It's clean, flexible, and the community is very responsive, so it's constantly improving at a fast pace... some default settings, like pagination and tag pages, can generate thousands of non-helpful pages [hurting SEO].
Maybe not fitting to mention that here, but Typora still doesn't support .mdx files out of the box. This makes maintaining docusaurus sites a hassle.
It's probably also a good thing that Facebook dogfoods Docusaurus in some places, while keeping it MIT licensed so the community can fork it if Facebook ever decides to stop maintaining it.

I tried migrating our markdown docs-as-code to use Docusaurus, we have somewhere around several hundred pages, and the build times seemed very long (5-10 minutes) compared to a simple bespoke python-based static site generator.

My company migrated away from docusaurus because at 1500+ markdown documents to index, the VM running it crashed out-of-memory. The VM has 32GB RAM allocated. Somehow, someway, it was very resource-intensive for what it was.

When I tried to create marketing pages with Starlight in addition to the technical documentation, I nearly gave up. Coming from the Docusaurus world, this wasn't an issue as the starter template comes with a front page and a blog out of the box.

I moved from 11ty / eleventy to docusaurus... Very active project. Nice theme out of the box / configuration. Better than any static site generator I've used thus far. React components. Configurability. The sidebar, which supports nesting.
